title: Satwik and Chirag Won Singapore. Now They Head to Jakarta. The Indonesia Open Starts Tuesday.
excerpt: India's doubles world-beaters carry a two-year title drought-ending high into the toughest draw in badminton, with PV Sindhu also eyeing a deep run at the BWF Super 1000 event.
body:
Five days after ending a two-year title drought at the Singapore Open, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will walk into the Istora Senayan in Jakarta for the Indonesia Open 2026 — the most prestigious stop on the BWF World Tour calendar, and the hardest draw in badminton.

The BWF Super 1000 event starts Tuesday, June 3, and the Indian contingent, led by the doubles pair and PV Sindhu in women's singles, has genuine reasons to believe this is their moment.

## The Singapore Breakthrough Changed the Narrative

When Satwik and Chirag came from a set down to beat Indonesia's Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Fikri 18-21, 21-17, 21-16 in the Singapore Open final on May 31, it was more than a title. It was vindication.

The pair had gone two years without a BWF World Tour trophy — a drought that had begun to fuel questions about whether their 2024 Paris Olympics campaign represented a peak rather than a platform. In Singapore, they found the answer. They became the first Indian doubles pair to win the Singapore Open, and they did it by playing their best badminton of the season — aggressive net play from Satwik, clinical finishing from Chirag, and a composure in the decider that had been missing earlier in the year.

## Indonesia Is a Different Beast

The Indonesia Open is badminton's spiritual home tournament. The Istora Senayan crowd is the loudest and most knowledgeable in the sport. The draw is stacked — every top-ten pair in the world enters, and the Indonesian pairs carry the weight of national expectation.

For Satwik and Chirag, that means an almost certain collision course with at least one Indonesian duo in the knockout rounds. In their Singapore Open final against Fajar and Fikri, the Indonesian crowd was subdued. In Jakarta, it will be anything but.

The conditions will be different too. The Istora Senayan court plays slightly slower, and the humidity demands peak fitness. The pair's conditioning will be tested over five matches in five days — the tax of back-to-back tournaments on the BWF circuit.

## Sindhu's Quiet Return to Form

While the doubles pair commands the headlines, PV Sindhu's Singapore campaign offered quieter encouragement. The two-time Olympic medallist defeated several higher-ranked opponents before falling to Olympic champion An Se-young of South Korea in the quarter-finals.

It was Sindhu's most consistent run in a BWF Super event since early 2025, and the Indonesia Open draw could offer a kinder path to the last eight. A deep run in Jakarta would be a significant marker ahead of the World Championships in August.

## What Makes This Week Different

Three factors set this Indonesia Open apart from recent editions:

**The momentum.** Satwik and Chirag arrive as the hottest pair on tour. Winning Singapore and immediately backing it up in Jakarta would place them alongside the great Malaysian and Indonesian pairs who once dominated the Asian swing.

**The Olympic cycle.** The 2028 Los Angeles Olympics qualifying window is now well open. Every Super 1000 result carries heavy points implications. A semifinal or better in Jakarta could significantly boost India's ranking position across all disciplines.

**The depth.** India will field entries in men's singles (Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy), women's singles (PV Sindhu, Aakarshi Kashyap), and men's doubles (Satwik/Chirag, Dhruv Kapila/MR Arjun). A decade ago, India was a one-discipline presence at BWF events. Not any more.

## For NRI Fans

The Indonesia Open broadcast in India will be on JioCinema and Sports18, with matches beginning at 10:30 AM IST on the opening day. For diaspora fans in Southeast Asia — particularly Jakarta's Indian community, estimated at over 50,000 — the tournament is the most accessible major of the year. Singapore Open success has already driven ticket demand from Indian-origin fans in the city.

The last Indian to win a BWF Super 1000 singles title was Sindhu at the 2019 World Championships. The last Indian pair to string together back-to-back Super event titles was nobody — it has never been done. Tuesday in Jakarta, the attempt begins.
author: Diaspora Desk
